to be saints. we can try to do this by following the message and example of jesus, as shown in the gospel. jesus teaches the disciples god’s law in a new way, summed up in the beatitudes, are a map with of eight different paths. by following them, we align our lives with the heart of god and ‘holiness’. the first reading gives us a vision of heaven. those who belong to the lord are marked with a seal and kept safe, ‘an innumerable number from every nation, from all tribes and peoples. in the second reading, john addresses us as ‘beloved’, reminding us that we are children of god. although today’s world may misunderstand god’s way, we are promised eternal life when we will see god as he is. the psalmist sings of the created world and all dwelling in it. those who seek the lord’s face with clean hands and a pure heart will receive his blessing. on this feast, let’s pray for all those persecuted for their faith; dates for your diary “holiness is not the luxury of the few; it is a simple duty for you and me.”st teresa of calcutta thought for the week the saints were ordinary people who let christ’s love conquer their weakness. which beatitude is jesus inviting me to live out more fully this week? to ponder this week men and women of the beatitudes hymns 10.30am mass, church of the holy child, whitehall opening hymn no.66, offertory hymn no.16 holy child nativity parishes beaumont | larkhill | whitehall | santry we lift our eyes to heaven to honour not only the known, canonised saints, but also the anonymous, quiet saints: the mothers and fathers who built society through daily devotion to their families, the priests and religious who were consumed like candles in service, and the missionaries who left everything to bring christ to the ends of the earth. this feast reminds us that holiness is a universal vocation—a beautiful, personal path that every baptised christian is uniquely capable of walking. the liturgy leads us up the mount of the beatitudes in the gospel of saint matthew, where jesus reveals the definitive blueprint for this journey. the beatitudes are the "magna charta" of the christian life. they turn worldly logic on its head, showing us that true happiness is found in meekness, purity of heart, mercy, and peacemaking. the saints are simply ordinary people who allowed themselves to become "men and women of the beatitudes," allowing christ's love to conquer human weakness. his sunday, we celebrate the solemnity of all saints, joining our hearts to the vast, uncountable multitude praised in the first reading from the apocalypse. in the light of the church's timeless teaching on this great feast, we are reminded that all saints' day is not just a commemoration of historical figures, but a vibrant thanksgiving for the wonders god has accomplished in human history through ordinary lives. year a | solemnity of all saints
